correctness.rationale: Black–De Loera Theorem 1.1(c,f) and Lemma 3.6 give the exact punctured-grid one-skeleton. The three-vertex-path Laplacian eigenvalues are zero, one, and three, producing the full-grid Kirchhoff product. The weighted rooted Laplacian minor yields an exact center-degree polynomial; its neighbor Green matrix decomposes under signed permutations into three invariant eigenspaces. Explicit pseudoinverse tensor evaluations give the two rational binomial parameters with their precise denominators. Counting trees where the center is a leaf supplies the exact central-degree correction. Binomial concentration yields both limits. The self-contained checker independently reconstructs graph cofactors for grid dimensions two, three, and four, verifies all displayed integer counts, and checks enough weighted determinants to identify the whole degree polynomial in each tested dimension. No finite check is used to prove an all-dimensional statement.

value.rationale: The signohedron gives a canonical natural graph, not an arbitrary parameter slice. Its spanning-tree complexity is a global connectivity invariant usually requiring an exponentially large matrix-tree cofactor. The derived exact product needs only binomial sums indexed by the coordinate dimension and a Cartesian eigenvalue product. The completely characterized local degree law for a uniform spanning tree of the central completion is a structural statement rather than a routine numerical instance. The ratio of the surviving tree count, scaled by twice the number of coordinates, to the original tree count converges to the reciprocal of Euler’s number, quantifying asymptotic robustness under deleting the natural forbidden sign vector. This limit is a consequence, not the sole value proposition.
